source.method: reuse prior authored editorial glosses; no new sense discovery claimed

candidates.gloss_en: to teach a worker new or updated skills
candidates.linguistic_reason: Machine-learning model retraining is a technical extension.

candidates.gloss_en: relating to ocean tides
candidates.linguistic_reason: Tidal modifies flow, forces or cycles caused by tides.

candidates.gloss_en: the act of overseeing work or conduct
candidates.linguistic_reason: Supervision can include mentoring guidance, but oversight is central.

candidates.gloss_en: an official who investigates certain deaths
candidates.linguistic_reason: Coroner's legal powers and qualifications vary across jurisdictions.

candidates.gloss_en: to bend a part of the body or a material
candidates.linguistic_reason: Flex also means contract a muscle and informally show off.

candidates.gloss_en: a very large amount of something
candidates.linguistic_reason: Abundance denotes plentiful supply, not necessarily high quality.

candidates.gloss_en: a box used to hold a dead body for burial
candidates.linguistic_reason: Coffin is a burial container; regional terms vary from casket.

candidates.gloss_en: a group of people or vehicles traveling together
candidates.linguistic_reason: British caravan for a mobile vacation trailer is a separate sense.

candidates.gloss_en: a person who predicts future conditions
candidates.linguistic_reason: Forecaster denotes a specialist making predictions, notably weather or economic forecasts.

candidates.gloss_en: alone and without companions
candidates.linguistic_reason: Solitary also implies lonely or secluded; physical aloneness differs from emotion.

candidates.gloss_en: moving regularly from one region to another
candidates.linguistic_reason: Migratory describes seasonal movement of animals or populations.

candidates.gloss_en: as large or great as possible under given conditions
candidates.linguistic_reason: Maximal denotes the greatest attainable extent, unlike merely very large.

candidates.gloss_en: to work very hard for a long time
candidates.linguistic_reason: Toil also denotes exhausting work as a noun; part of speech unresolved.

candidates.gloss_en: with regard to money or finance
candidates.linguistic_reason: Financially concerns money, income, and funds; not general efficiency.

candidates.gloss_en: a small island, especially in literary names
candidates.linguistic_reason: Isle is poetic or traditional compared with island.

candidates.gloss_en: cloth woven from flax fibers
candidates.linguistic_reason: Linen also collectively denotes bed or table textiles of various fabrics.

candidates.gloss_en: parallel to the horizon
candidates.linguistic_reason: Horizontal describes orientation, not necessarily a flat physical surface.

candidates.gloss_en: not permitted or justified by law or accepted rules
candidates.linguistic_reason: Illegitimate historically described nonmarital birth, a stigmatizing context requiring separate sense.

candidates.gloss_en: relating to a larva or larvae
candidates.linguistic_reason: Larval is the adjective for a developmental stage, not mature insects.

candidates.gloss_en: a line of police or guards controlling access to an area
candidates.linguistic_reason: Cordon is a controlled barrier; culinary cordon meanings differ.

candidates.gloss_en: with a high level of practical ability
candidates.linguistic_reason: Skillfully emphasizes competent execution, not mere speed.

candidates.gloss_en: to send something in a different direction
candidates.linguistic_reason: Divert also means distract attention, entertain, or redirect funds.

candidates.gloss_en: energy and lively enthusiasm
candidates.linguistic_reason: Pep is informal and typically names spirited energy.

candidates.gloss_en: relating to weather and its scientific study
candidates.linguistic_reason: Meteorological concerns atmospheric weather, not geology.

candidates.gloss_en: produced independently of major commercial organizations
candidates.linguistic_reason: Indie may be adjective or noun for a creator or label; music and games contexts differ.

candidates.gloss_en: an informal name given to someone instead of their real name
candidates.linguistic_reason: Nickname is a substitute familiar name, distinct from a legal name.

candidates.gloss_en: to express or represent a quality or idea concretely
candidates.linguistic_reason: Embody makes an abstract ideal or property manifest, not mere physical containment.

candidates.gloss_en: money offered as a reward for capturing or finding someone
candidates.linguistic_reason: Bounty also means generous plenty; reward sense needs separation.

candidates.gloss_en: a person driving a car or another motor vehicle
candidates.linguistic_reason: Motorist denotes road vehicle driver, not every traveler.

candidates.gloss_en: a written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation
candidates.linguistic_reason: Affidavit is a sworn legal document; procedure varies by jurisdiction.

candidates.gloss_en: to make a low sound expressing pain or displeasure
candidates.linguistic_reason: Groan also functions as a noun; verb sense selected.

candidates.gloss_en: to feel deep sorrow after a loss
candidates.linguistic_reason: Grieve is often intransitive; to grieve someone can be transitive in some contexts.

candidates.gloss_en: to cause something to happen
candidates.linguistic_reason: Induce also means persuade or trigger medically; causation core but mechanisms vary.

candidates.gloss_en: a container or device that keeps things cool
candidates.linguistic_reason: Cooler also is comparative adjective and slang for jail, requiring POS separation.

candidates.gloss_en: the movement of liquid, money, or people out of a place
candidates.linguistic_reason: Outflow can denote process or quantity, a closely connected pair.

candidates.gloss_en: not completely; to some extent
candidates.linguistic_reason: Partially restricts extent rather than probability.

candidates.gloss_en: to take property from someone by force or threat
candidates.linguistic_reason: Rob typically takes a person or place as object, unlike steal taking the object.

candidates.gloss_en: to bring a feeling or memory into someone's mind
candidates.linguistic_reason: Evoke typically governs feelings, memories, or images, not physically summon objects.

candidates.gloss_en: a hormone that helps regulate glucose in the blood
candidates.linguistic_reason: Insulin is a pancreatic hormone and treatment medication; hormone concept central.

candidates.gloss_en: to take one number or quantity away from another
candidates.linguistic_reason: Subtract denotes arithmetic deduction and typically uses from.

candidates.gloss_en: occurring after a war, especially a major war
candidates.linguistic_reason: Postwar is an adjective about a period following conflict.

candidates.gloss_en: to understand something difficult after thinking carefully
candidates.linguistic_reason: Fathom also names a nautical depth unit, separate noun sense.

candidates.gloss_en: an area designated for people to camp
candidates.linguistic_reason: Campground is chiefly US English for campsite grounds.

candidates.gloss_en: a disease outbreak affecting many people in a region
candidates.linguistic_reason: Epidemic also is adjective and figurative widespread problem; epidemiological noun sense chosen.

candidates.gloss_en: financial or other support supplied by a sponsor
candidates.linguistic_reason: Sponsorship also implies formal responsibility or advocacy, varying by domain.

candidates.gloss_en: the part of a scene nearest the observer
candidates.linguistic_reason: Foreground as verb means emphasize; noun scene sense differs.

candidates.gloss_en: a long tube in the body in which food is digested and absorbed
candidates.linguistic_reason: Intestine refers to small or large bowel, distinct from stomach.

candidates.gloss_en: an official who enforces rules in a sports contest
candidates.linguistic_reason: Umpire especially applies to cricket, baseball or tennis, not all sports interchangeably.

candidates.gloss_en: to take something apart into its separate pieces
candidates.linguistic_reason: Dismantle also figuratively means end a system or organization.

candidates.gloss_en: an area equipped for aircraft to take off and land
candidates.linguistic_reason: Airfield need not have the full infrastructure of a major airport.

candidates.gloss_en: to officially end a law, institution, or practice
candidates.linguistic_reason: Abolish implies formal removal of established institutions or systems.

candidates.gloss_en: a series of three connected literary or artistic works
candidates.linguistic_reason: Trilogy is three related works, not simply any three unrelated items.

candidates.gloss_en: a person using or living in a place
candidates.linguistic_reason: Occupant is neutral and does not imply ownership or tenancy.

candidates.gloss_en: made of metal or resembling metal
candidates.linguistic_reason: Metallic also describes ringing sounds or taste; physical and sensory senses differ.

candidates.gloss_en: at right angles to a level surface
candidates.linguistic_reason: Vertical can also describe organizational hierarchy, a metaphorical extension.

candidates.gloss_en: to make someone or something seem worthy of respect
candidates.linguistic_reason: Dignify commonly occurs in 'dignify with a response'; connotation may be ironic.

candidates.gloss_en: to wind audio or video recording back to an earlier position
candidates.linguistic_reason: Rewind also figuratively means return to earlier events and is a noun in some contexts.

candidates.gloss_en: a person who enters somewhere without permission
candidates.linguistic_reason: Intruder implies unauthorized entry, including digital-system intrusion.

candidates.gloss_en: solid waste discharged from the intestines
candidates.linguistic_reason: Feces is a plural-form mass noun in medical contexts; US spelling differs from faeces.

candidates.gloss_en: a man who does manual or skilled work
candidates.linguistic_reason: Workman is gendered and may sound dated compared with worker.

candidates.gloss_en: with strong interest or enthusiasm
candidates.linguistic_reason: Eagerly describes anticipation or willingness rather than anxiety.

candidates.gloss_en: the state of being too crowded or blocked
candidates.linguistic_reason: Traffic congestion differs from congestion of blood or nasal tissue.

candidates.gloss_en: to apply force, influence, or effort
candidates.linguistic_reason: Exert commonly takes pressure, effort, influence or control as object.

candidates.gloss_en: to adjust a measuring instrument to a known standard
candidates.linguistic_reason: Calibrate involves comparing to reference, not merely configuring a device.

candidates.gloss_en: to state again that a belief or commitment remains valid
candidates.linguistic_reason: Reaffirm stresses renewed assertion or endorsement.

candidates.gloss_en: a very small drop of liquid
candidates.linguistic_reason: Droplet is a diminutive liquid drop, not an aerosol category by definition.

candidates.gloss_en: a person held in custody, especially without a criminal conviction
candidates.linguistic_reason: Detainee denotes detention status; does not establish guilt.

candidates.gloss_en: to cause severe and extensive damage to something
candidates.linguistic_reason: Ravage is strongly negative and generally denotes widespread devastation.

candidates.gloss_en: to restore someone to a former position or status
candidates.linguistic_reason: Reinstate may also restore a rule, benefit or policy, requiring object context.

candidates.gloss_en: a small songbird known for singing while flying
candidates.linguistic_reason: Lark as a playful activity is a distinct informal sense.

candidates.gloss_en: to change from liquid into vapor
candidates.linguistic_reason: Evaporate also figuratively means vanish unexpectedly.

candidates.gloss_en: uncertain or slow to act because of doubt
candidates.linguistic_reason: Hesitant is about reluctance or uncertainty, not merely slow action.

candidates.gloss_en: to call on a rule or authority for support
candidates.linguistic_reason: Computing invoke means execute a function, separate technical sense.

candidates.gloss_en: having a great deal of information or expertise
candidates.linguistic_reason: Knowledgeable usually means informed about a subject, not omniscient.

candidates.gloss_en: relating to or caused by bacteria
candidates.linguistic_reason: Bacterial infection refers to bacteria, not all microbes.

candidates.gloss_en: to examine something very closely and carefully
candidates.linguistic_reason: Scrutinize emphasizes detailed critical inspection.

candidates.gloss_en: to remove a government or ruler from power
candidates.linguistic_reason: Overthrow also describes physically knocking something down.

candidates.gloss_en: the freedom to decide how to act in a particular situation
candidates.linguistic_reason: Discretion also means tact and care in handling secrets.

candidates.gloss_en: people of high social standing below the nobility, historically
candidates.linguistic_reason: Gentry is a historically and regionally specific class term.

candidates.gloss_en: to alter information or records dishonestly
candidates.linguistic_reason: Falsify also means disprove a proposition in scientific reasoning.

candidates.gloss_en: a railway system or railway line, especially in American English
candidates.linguistic_reason: Railroad noun is chiefly US; verb can mean force someone unfairly.

candidates.gloss_en: to make an image or object appear to move
candidates.linguistic_reason: Animate also means give life or energy to a person or discussion.

candidates.gloss_en: relating to a large city and its surrounding area
candidates.linguistic_reason: Metropolitan includes an urban region, not just the city center.

candidates.gloss_en: expected to happen soon
candidates.linguistic_reason: Upcoming refers to future scheduled or anticipated events.

candidates.gloss_en: the rate or extent to which something is adopted
candidates.linguistic_reason: Biological absorption and uptake of information are separate contexts.

candidates.gloss_en: by careful evaluation of evidence and arguments
candidates.linguistic_reason: Critically also means severely or vitally, different sense.

candidates.gloss_en: having an uneven surface with rocks or rough features
candidates.linguistic_reason: Rugged can also describe durable equipment or a tough appearance.

candidates.gloss_en: to persuade someone into sexual activity or tempt them into wrongdoing
candidates.linguistic_reason: Seduce may concern sexual persuasion or general enticement; contexts require care.

candidates.gloss_en: a small sweet red fruit with seeds on its outer surface
candidates.linguistic_reason: Strawberry is the familiar culinary fruit; botany classifies structure differently.

candidates.gloss_en: a flying insect with a narrow waist that may sting
candidates.linguistic_reason: Wasp covers many related insects and differs from bees.

candidates.gloss_en: to use up money, time, or energy
candidates.linguistic_reason: Expend commonly takes resources or effort, usually formal.

candidates.gloss_en: a steroid hormone involved in the menstrual cycle and pregnancy
candidates.linguistic_reason: Progesterone is a hormone, not identical to every synthetic progestin.

candidates.gloss_en: an official list or system used to record information
candidates.linguistic_reason: Registry can denote office, list or computer configuration store.

candidates.gloss_en: to strongly disapprove of or regret something
candidates.linguistic_reason: Deplore takes an action or situation as object; not simple sadness.

candidates.gloss_en: physically weak or easily damaged
candidates.linguistic_reason: Frail can describe people or fragile structures; semantic extensions need context.

candidates.gloss_en: a noncommissioned officer rank in military or police organizations
candidates.linguistic_reason: Rank and duties vary by service and jurisdiction.

candidates.gloss_en: relating to organisms and their environment
candidates.linguistic_reason: Ecological is not identical to environmentally friendly.

candidates.gloss_en: a small electronic device that receives short alerts or messages
candidates.linguistic_reason: Pager was widely used before mobile phones; still used in some workplaces.

candidates.gloss_en: the act of allocating something or an allocated share
candidates.linguistic_reason: British allotment also means a small rented garden plot.

candidates.gloss_en: not often seen or encountered
candidates.linguistic_reason: Uncommon may also praise exceptional qualities, a distinct evaluative nuance.
